title: Detection by upper-bounded approximations
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $B$ be an abelian category with an unbounded derived category [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Let $F,G:D(R)\to D(B)$ be triangulated functors with their shift compatibilities, and let $\tau:F\Rightarrow G$ be a natural transformation. Fix $M\in D(R)$ and $d\in\mathbf Z$. Assume that for every $c\in\mathbf Z$ and $E\in D(R)$ with $H^i(E)=0$ for $i>c$, both $F(E)$ and $G(E)$ have zero cohomology in degrees greater than $c+d$. Suppose also that for every integer $c$ there is a distinguished triangle
$$P\longrightarrow M\longrightarrow C\longrightarrow P[1]$$
such that $H^i(C)=0$ for $i>c$ and $\tau_P$ is an isomorphism. Then $\tau_M$ is an isomorphism. Compatibility of $\tau$ itself with shifts is not assumed.

proof.text:
in degree r choose an approximation with cone bound r-d-2. After either functor,
the cone vanishes in degrees r-1 and r. The long exact sequences make both approximation
maps invertible in degree r. Naturality and the isomorphism at the approximation make
the desired map invertible in degree r. Cohomological detection finishes the proof.

lean.statement:
theorem isIso_app_of_approximations
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ModuleCat.{u} R)]
    {B : Type v} [Category B] [Abelian B] [HasDerivedCategory B]
    (F G : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} R) ⥤ DerivedCategory B)
    [F.CommShift ℤ] [G.CommShift ℤ] [F.IsTriangulated] [G.IsTriangulated]
    (τ : F ⟶ G) (M : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} R)) (d : ℤ)
    (hF : ∀ (E : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} R)) (c : ℤ), E.IsLE c →
      (F.obj E).IsLE (c + d))
    (hG : ∀ (E : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} R)) (c : ℤ), E.IsLE c →
      (G.obj E).IsLE (c + d))
    (happrox : ∀ c : ℤ, ∃ T : Triangle (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} R)),
      T ∈ distTriang _ ∧ T.obj₂ = M ∧ T.obj₃.IsLE c ∧ IsIso (τ.app T.obj₁)) :
    IsIso (τ.app M)
